title: Pre-participation Cardiovascular Screening of Young Competitive Athletes: Policy Guidance
claims: The AHA recommends that competitive athlete pre-participation screening happen annually and consist of a targeted personal history, family history and physical examination using 14 key elements.

At the time of the document, the AHA did not recommend a mandatory 12-lead ECG or echocardiogram in pre-participation screening; these tests are used as follow-up when initial screening raises suspicion.
Estimates of sudden cardiac death incidence among high school athletes range from 1 in 23,000 to 1 in 300,000.

False-positive rates for physician-read athlete ECGs generally range from 1.3% to 2.8%, but can be as high as 6.8% in Arab and Black athletes; computer-read ECGs have false-positive rates from 2.3% to 5%.
The false-negative rate of 12-lead ECG for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy has been reported as 10%.
A prospective trial of high school students found that the AHA 14-element screening performed less well than ECG for cardiovascular screening.
license: American Heart Association; citation and summary only
